correction.text: Kars (Vanand), the Bagratid sub-kingdom at Kars

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 963-1064. The page gives the capital and says Kars was 'always in the possession of the relatives of the rulers of Ani'; it names no frontier and no area, so Kars province (41 grid cells, about 10,400 km2 on the gazetteer) is the reading shared with the Bagratid Armenia dossier. Ardahan and Shirak are not on the page.

ledger.note: 963: Mushegh founds the Kingdom of Kars (Vanand). The kingdom was 'formed in the year 963 by the son of Abas I of Armenia', capital Kars.

1065: Gagik-Abas cedes Kars to the Byzantine Empire. 'In 1064, just after the capture of Ani by Alp Arslan', he paid homage to the Seljuks so they would not besiege Kars, but 'In 1065 Gagik-Abas ceded his kingdom to the Byzantine Empire'; Kars was taken by the Seljuks 'soon after'.
1065: the Kingdom of Kars ends with the cession to Byzantium (infobox range 963-1064).

wars.name: Seljuk pressure on Kars
wars.outcome: After Alp Arslan took Ani in 1064 Gagik-Abas paid homage to the Seljuks to spare Kars, then ceded the kingdom to Byzantium in 1065; the Seljuks took Kars soon after.
wars.note: Ani was surrendered to the Byzantines in 1045, after which the title 'King of Kings' passed to the ruler of Kars (page).

certainty.note: No boundary on the page; the province of Kars is a soft reading.

sources.title: Kingdom of Kars
sources.note: Founding 963, Gagik-Abas 1064/1065, capital; no area, no extent, rulers thin.

notes: No Cliopatria row. Page budget one page (the state has no shapes). The page does not give the extent or Gagik-Abas's reign (1029-1064 appears only in other sources), so nothing is dated from memory. The byzantine-empire dossier dates the cession 1064 (no year on the page it used) and the Seljuk capture 1065; this page has the cession in 1065 and the Seljuk capture 'soon after'. Bagratid Armenia records Kars as a vassal from 963 to 1045 (counterpart kingdom-of-kars). After 1045 the Kars ruler held the title King of Kings (page). Unclear how independent Kars was from Ani (page). wikidata null.
